findings.reason: without naming the lazy re-export (the `import_module` idiom `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:75` already uses) or moving the constants beside `crew/pace.py`, the plan's own criterion is applied to one candidate and not to the one it selects, and the chosen home can be unbuildable as written.
findings.text: §2 rejects `crew/pace.py` because budget.py imports it at module level and the family reads budget.py, so hosting the family there would make `crew/pace.py` import `reckon.budget` — a cycle; but after the cut `reckon/pace_report.py` still needs budget.py's module-level clock and window constants (`CLOCK_FIVE_HOUR`, `CLOCK_SEVEN_DAY`, `OBSERVED`, `UNKNOWN`, `WINDOW_SOURCE_RECORDED`, budget.py:2379–2397, none of which is in the moved set), and line 55 requires every moved public name to stay importable from `reckon.budget`, so budget.py must import `reckon.pace_report` — the same back-import, which is a cycle at import time and an `ImportError` for a worker who writes it at the top of budget.py as the file imports its other siblings; §2 names a lazy import only for the verdict into `budget_lift.py` (line 53), never for the new module.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — f5e88d284, 6ebe65ba4 and 76946f9a9 all resolve; budget.py reproduces at 180,363 bytes / 51,533 tokens (f5e88d284) and 197,708 bytes / 56,488 tokens (76946f9a9), budget_lift.py at 14,536 tokens, 6ebe65ba4^ at 50,293 tokens; all fifteen named family symbols exist as module-level definitions in budget.py at f5e88d284; DEFAULT_CREDIT_RESERVE_FRACTION is at budget_lift.py:113; followup f-lamr-053 exists and is open; the extensionless href /reckon/every-module-fits-a-worker-window resolves as docs/plans/every-module-fits-a-worker-window.html.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s2's done-when measures the width test's offender list at the node's head, a ≤45,000-token bound on budget.py and a ≤40,000 bound on each other touched module, the remaining offenders against the base arm, and a 16-file gate run at base and head that adds no failure, and it declares a negative control (restore budget.py's base content in a scratch copy and the width test must name it again).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the only scratch tree s2 names is the negative control's copy of base budget.py, which is a measurement tree rather than the evidence store; gate and base-arm logs land in the run directory under the dispatch contract, and no session-scratchpad or node-local path is named as evidence.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `reckon/pace_report.py` names the capability it adds (the report, row and hold composed over crew/pace.py's allowance), and no plan label, stage name or ticket id reaches the new module, symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the cycle argument that rules out crew/pace.py as the family's home (budget.py imports it at module level, and the family reads budget.py's state, so hosting the family there would make crew/pace.py import reckon.budget) applies unchanged to the home the plan chooses.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: the pace and lift family leaves budget.py, with its re-exports, its test repoints and its citation follow-on as consequences of that one move.
